Given data:
- Feed flow rate (F) = 100 kmol/h.
- Component composition and relative volatilities (α):

| Component | z_F | α |
|---|---|---|
| Propane | 0.05 | 4.2 |
| n-butane (light key) | 0.35 | 2.0 |
| n-pentane (heavy key) | 0.40 | 1.0 |
| n-hexane | 0.20 | 0.45 |

The recovery rates are:
- 98% of n-butane in the distillate.
- 97% of n-pentane in the bottoms.

### Part (a): Calculate the distillate flow rate (D)
Using the component material balance:
\[ x_D^{n-butane} = 0.98z_F^{n-butane} \]
\[ x_D^{n-pentane} = (1-0.97)z_F^{n-pentane} = 0.03z_F^{n-pentane} \]

The moles of n-butane in distillate (D_B):
\[ D_B = 0.98 \times 0.35 \times F \]
\[ D_B = 0.98 \times 0.35 \times 100 \]
\[ D_B = 34.3 \text{ kmol/h} \]

Similarly, moles of n-pentane in distillate (D_P):
\[ D_P = 0.03 \times 0.40 \times F \]
\[ D_P = 0.03 \times 0.40 \times 100 \]
\[ D_P = 1.2 \text{ kmol/h} \]

Since all propane goes to distillate and all n-hexane to bottoms:
\[ D_{propane} = 0.05 \times F \]
\[ D_{propane} = 0.05 \times 100 \]
\[ D_{propane} = 5 \text{ kmol/h} \]

Thus, total distillate flow rate (D):
\[ D = D_B + D_P + D_{propane} + (Other negligible) \]
\[ D = 34.3 + 1.2 + 5 \]
\[ D = 40.5 \text{ kmol/h} \]

FINAL (a): 40.5 kmol/h
